links.outcome: Performance across training/test years, model longevity and effect of annual retraining
links.effect: Performance on future test sets varied between AUROC 0.64 and 0.76 depending on training years; older data still yielded reasonable performance, and later added recent data did not necessarily raise performance.
links.quote: The results from the sliding window experiment highlight that depending on which years (fixed training sample size, n = 3000) the model is trained, performance on the future test sets varies considerably, ranging between AUROCs of 0.64 and 0.76.

links.outcome: Temporal drift in features, labels and patient population between training and later years
links.effect: Label ratio stayed overall stable, but top features varied strongly over time (e.g., therapy goal, albumin); authors describe moderate drift, with performance decreasing slightly.
links.quote: The heatmap displays large variations for almost all top features.

links.outcome: Effect of data valuation pruning and feature reduction on prospective performance
links.effect: Data values declined sharply before 2014; final model trained on 2014-2020 data with 405 of 1050 features and tested on independent 2022 set, with comparable performance across the three models.
links.quote: Supplementary Fig. S3 shows comparable performance of all three models (LASSO, XGBoost, and RF) in three configurations: when trained i) on full data, ii) upon data pruning, i.e., after removing the years with the lowest data value averages (2010–2013), and iii) upon data pruning and permutation importance-based feature reduction.
